title: Symmetry-Constrained Chirped Defect Cavity with Gradient Penalty (21 Layers)
scientific_hypothesis: A 21-layer symmetric defect-cavity filter with bounded ±8% chirp envelope, frozen outermost 4 layers for impedance matching, and gradient penalty >15% will recover the 0.9831 score while improving convergence stability compared to unconstrained optimization.
design_principle: Quarter-wave DBR mirrors (Ta2O5/SiO2) with half-wave defect cavity at 1550 nm, chirped thickness initialization within ±8% of nominal, hard symmetry constraints on layers 1-4 and 18-21, optimizer restricted to central 13 layers (5-17), penalty term for adjacent layer thickness gradients exceeding 15%.
proposed_topology: Air | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 (cavity) | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Fused Silica (21 finite layers: 10 DBR pairs + 1 cavity)
design_variables: thickness bounds: nominal ±8% for chirped layers, frozen for layers 1-4 and 18-21
soft_objectives: maintain thickness gradient <15% between adjacent layers
manufacturing_considerations: frozen outer layers simplify deposition monitoring
gradient penalty reduces risk of thickness discontinuities
theory_basis: Defective DBR bandpass filter theory: (HL)^N D(LH)^N structure creates transmission peak at defect mode wavelength
Quarter-wave optical thickness n*d = lambda0/4 for DBR, half-wave n*d = lambda0/2 for cavity
Symmetry constraints preserve input/output impedance matching
expected_advantages: Frozen outer layers stabilize convergence by preserving boundary conditions
Gradient penalty prevents optimizer from creating physically unrealistic thickness jumps
±8% chirp envelope provides exploration space while maintaining manufacturability
known_risks: Over-constraining optimizer may prevent escape from local optimum
Gradient penalty may conflict with spectral objectives if optimal solution requires sharp transitions
execution_request_english: Design a 21-layer Ta2O5/SiO2 defect-cavity bandpass filter on fused silica substrate for 1550 nm LiDAR. Layer sequence: Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5 (cavity), SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5, SiO2, Ta2O5. Initialize layers 1-4 and 18-21 to quarter-wave nominal thicknesses at 1550 nm (Ta2O5: 185 nm, SiO2: 267 nm) and freeze these 8 layers during optimization. Initialize central 13 layers (5-17) with quarter-wave/half-wave nominal values plus bounded chirp perturbation within ±8%. Cavity layer (layer 11) nominal half-wave thickness 534 nm with bounds 400-650 nm. Optimize layers 5-17 using gradient-based thickness optimizer with penalty term for adjacent layer thickness gradients exceeding 15%. Evaluate transmittance at normal incidence, unpolarized, across 1400-1700 nm. Target: maximize transmittance at 1550 nm, suppress 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm bands. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1400-1500 nm, 1550-1550 nm, 1600-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance at 1550 nm (soft target ≥ 0.95); strong suppression of transmittance in 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 1400-1500 nm; transmittance in 1600-1700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30.
revision_reason: Implements feedback directives: ±8% chirp envelope, frozen outermost 4 layers per side for impedance matching, optimizer restricted to central 13 layers, gradient penalty >15%. Differs from prior 21L routes by adding explicit symmetry constraints and gradient regularization to address score regression observed in iterations 20 and 24.
